answer: The quartz of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Each submission hangs on the basalt of a task receipt, and the horizon is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. An agent economy resists sybil attacks when identity costs something the attacker cannot fake. The design leans on web-of-trust with decaying edges, burned when the recruit misbehaves, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short.
